result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_mutual_node_pairs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count mutual node pairs (bidirectional edges) in directed graphs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14353-L14437){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_mutual_node_pairs() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Count mutual node pairs](/assets/graphs/count-mutual-node-pairs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared graph, directed. A and B point at each other, and so do C and D; those reciprocal arcs are in the accent color and the one-way edges are faded. The card counts the two mutual pairs." width="100%"} Returns the number of node pairs `(a,b)` where both edges `a->b` and `b->a` exist. Each such pair is counted once, not once per direction. Self-loops are excluded. Together with `count_asymmetric_node_pairs()`, this describes the dyads of a directed network: every pair of nodes is either mutual, asymmetric (one-way), or unconnected. Mutual pairs measure reciprocity, which is central to the analysis of directed networks such as: - social networks (do people follow each other back?) - communication or trade networks (are flows two-way?) - citation or hyperlink networks, where reciprocity is usually rare A common summary is the dyad-based reciprocity `mutual / (mutual + asymmetric)`, the share of connected pairs that are linked in both directions. Parallel edges don't change the count: a pair with three `A->B` edges and one `B->A` edge is still one mutual pair. The count covers the whole graph and ignores the current selection. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of node pairs with edges in both directions. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Only the `A`/`B` pair has edges running both ways, so it's the only mutual pair counted -- the one-way `A -> C` edge doesn't contribute: ::: {#192cb6b6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("B", "A"), # mutual with A -> B ("A", "C"), # one-way only ] ) ) graph.count_mutual_node_pairs() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Combined with `count_asymmetric_node_pairs()`, the count gives the dyad-based reciprocity of a small "follows" network. Two of the four connected pairs follow each other, so the reciprocity is `0.5`: ::: {#b92a2c44 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} follows = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["Ana", "Ben", "Cy", "Di"]) .add_edges( [ ("Ana", "Ben"), ("Ben", "Ana"), ("Cy", "Di"), ("Di", "Cy"), ("Ana", "Cy"), ("Di", "Ben"), ] ) ) mutual = follows.count_mutual_node_pairs() asymmetric = follows.count_asymmetric_node_pairs() mutual, asymmetric, mutual / (mutual + asymmetric) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (2, 2, 0.5) ``` ::: :::
